requirements.requirement: node2 can reach node3 on TCP port 5432 across the lan-a/lan-b boundary
requirements.summary: Direct socket connect test from node2 (10.50.10.11) to node3 (10.50.20.12:5432) with a listener on node3 succeeded and received data, both right after the final Ansible playbook run and again after all four nodes had been individually rebooted (post-reboot recheck cmd-30a091035/cmd-453d1fb7).

requirements.requirement: All other traffic between lan-a and lan-b (other ports, ICMP, reverse direction) is rejected
requirements.summary: node2->node3:8080 timed out, ICMP ping node2->node3 showed 100% loss, and the reverse direction (node3->node2:5432) timed out, both before and after the reboot cycle. nftables VYOS_FORWARD_filter chain shows accept established/related, accept tcp/5432 eth1->eth2, and a counting default drop rule, matching config.boot.

A playbook (cross-lan-firewall.yml) with inventory.ini staged on the control node (node4) addresses node2/node3 via nmcli tasks, configures firewalld on node3 via firewall-cmd tasks, and applies the VyOS router config via an ansible shell task (with become/sudo) since the community.vyos collection could not be installed offline. The playbook ran successfully end-to-end and idempotently (firewalld task skipped on second run) and was re-run successfully from node4 after node4's own reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node (independent of task contract)
requirements.summary: All four nodes show a pre-restart boot_id, a restart acknowledgement (reboot command), a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered state: node1's VyOS interfaces/firewall/nftables rules persisted in config.boot; node2/node3 network config and firewalld rules recovered; node4's ansible tooling and playbook files survived and a full playbook re-run against node1-3 succeeded post-reboot. A live end-to-end connectivity re-test (5432 allowed, ICMP blocked) after all reboots confirms functional recovery, not just configuration presence.

overall_summary: The Ansible playbook and VyOS/firewalld configuration satisfy the task contract: node2 can reach node3 on tcp/5432, and all other inter-LAN traffic (other ports, ICMP, reverse direction) is blocked, verified both immediately after the final playbook run and again after all four managed nodes were individually rebooted and recovered. The executor's provider-wide restart evidence protocol was completed for all nodes with boot_id transitions, config persistence, and a live post-reboot connectivity re-test. Extensive trial-and-error was needed to work around a VyOS cli-shell-api bug, producing a number of bounded mutations, nearly all of which were reverted; one inert leftover SSH key on node1's root account is a minor, low-risk residue.
limitations: The final VyOS task in the playbook uses a raw shell/vbash script (via become/sudo) rather than a native VyOS Ansible module, and its changed_when logic always reports 'changed' unless a hard failure string is present, so true no-op idempotency of that specific task cannot be confirmed from evidence, though the second playbook run's overall behavior (firewalld task skipping) shows partial idempotency.

Node2 and node3's own individual post-reboot recovery checks (immediately after their reboot commands) did not include a live 5432/ICMP connectivity test; that full connectivity re-verification only occurred later, after node1's reboot, at which point node2 and node3 had already been rebooted, so the evidence establishes recovery via a slightly indirect but still coherent chain rather than an immediate per-node check.

The large volume of diagnostic commands (207 total, 35 failed) made it difficult to fully trace every transient state change; a few earlier VyOS commit attempts with invalid values are visible but did not appear to persist any inconsistent state given the final delete-and-rebuild of the router config.
Operational hygiene cited unknown evidence IDs: cmd-74a467ead1,cmd-89ef58222acb4002

operational_hygiene.summary: Most of the 207 commands were read-only diagnostics working around a VyOS cli-shell-api session bug; the eventual fix (become/sudo on the VyOS shell task) was reasonable. Several bounded, low-risk mutations were made and later reverted: an unneeded firewalld port-5432 opening on node2 (cmd-74a467ead1, a client node that should never need inbound 5432) was removed shortly after (cmd-89ef582); multiple temporary python socket listeners on node2/node3 used for connectivity testing were all killed with pkill after use; stale /opt/vyatta/config/tmp session directories left behind by the executor's own repeated failed cli-shell-api setupSession experiments were cleaned up (cmd-a4be21c589e84bec, cmd-60a3190c). One low-risk item was not reverted: a cluster SSH public key was added to node1's /root/.ssh/authorized_keys (cmd-5b58fc18483144bf) while chasing root-login troubleshooting; this key remains but is inert since node1's active sshd_config denies root login (PermitRootLogin no), so it grants no actual access. The interim node1 VyOS firewall/interface config built during troubleshooting (cmd-2d8e5a4c...cmd-e8272938) was fully deleted (cmd-9d5d3b5c9a504989e) before the final Ansible-driven configuration was applied, leaving no conflicting residue.
